messages:
jen: Heads-up: ACME (kelly) seeing a sharp spike in 503s for hosted inference when using streaming + their token rotation. They say SDK retries immediately and are worried about duplicated billing. Attaching initial notes.
kelly-customer: repro steps: 1) create streaming request to /v1/generate with chunked body 2) set auth token rotation every 50ms (we do aggressive short-lived tokens) 3) observe ~1-2% 503s normally but this morning jumped to ~30% for a 10m window. Logs show `upstream response 503` and `http2: stream closed` then SDK retries right away. sample x-request-id: acme-20260317-9f7e.
jen: thanks. I've created this thread and tagged eng-oncall. Can someone triage?
devon: I'll take a look. quick question: are they on our hosted default edge pool or EU-dedicated?
kelly-customer: hosted default (usw2). No custom routing.
devon: ok. can you paste the raw error chunk (headers + connection error) when it happens? especially any `via`/`x-upstream` headers.
kelly-customer: paste: ```
HTTP/2 503
content-type: text/plain
via: 1.1 edge-proxy
x-request-id: acme-20260317-9f7e

upstream error: connection reset by peer
```
kelly-customer: and client log: `stream error: stream ID 21; PROTOCOL_ERROR` then our SDK does immediate retry (we use the default SDK retry settings).
ryan: pinging in-call. grabbing traces for acme-20260317-9f7e. initial observation: multiple concurrent auth refreshes from same tenant around that window. Could be token rotation fanout causing transient spikes at the edge.
alyssa: is this similar to prior auth-fanout issues? we had fix ideas: add jitter to token rotations and throttle auth calls at ingress.
devon: I'm seeing a correlation with HTTP/2 connection queueing. When many streams hit a single upstream connection and the upstream starts returning 5xx, the edge will reset some streams which manifests as 503s and stream resets. If clients then retry immediately (no jitter/backoff) it amplifies the load.
ryan: repro plan: 1) emulate ~200 concurrent streaming streams from one tenant with token rotation every 50ms 2) watch edge qlength, upstream 5xx, and client retries. I can repro locally with a small harness.
devon: short-term mitigations we can try: - add 100-300ms jitter to SDK immediate retry (ask customer to bump) - temporarily increase keepalive and connection window on edge to reduce resets - add a token-refresh throttle on ingress for suspicious high-frequency rotations
jen: which of these can we push quickly? customer is getting charged and wants a mitigation asap.
ryan: I can push an edge config tweak (increase http2 max concurrent streams per connection and adjust keepalive) to a canary pool in 15-30m. It'll require a config rollout.
devon: also recommend we tell customer to set SDK retry to exponential backoff + jitter in the next hour. that's the least invasive.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: edge-config-canary: increase http2.max_concurrent_streams=250, keepalive=90s. triggered by ryan. rollout id: rollout-20260317-rc1.
devon: I instrumented a short test: with the config change locally, the number of stream resets drops significantly under the same token rotation noise. Not a full fix but promising.
ryan: canary rollout complete for 10% of edge traffic (canary pool). monitoring p95 503 for tenant ACME now.
jen: customer update drafted: "we've identified a short-term cause (token-refresh fanout + HTTP/2 queueing). We rolled a canary edge config that reduces resets. Please try to enable exponential jitter on SDK retries; we'll follow up with a permanent fix." Want me to send?
kelly-customer: yes please — also, could you set a temporary flag on our tenant to route to canary if possible?
ryan: gave ACME canary flag (routing tag acme-canary-20260317) — they should start hitting canary in ~60s.
jen: sent message: "We deployed a targeted canary tweak to reduce stream resets and asked you to add retry jitter. We'll monitor and follow up with credits if needed."
deploy-bot: monitor alert: acme p95 503 decreased from 32% -> 3% in first 10m post-canary.
devon: that's encouraging. next steps (medium-term): - add server-side token refresh coalescing/throttling to prevent auth fanout - improve SDK default retry policy to include jitter and faster detection of unrecoverable stream resets - long-term: connection pool improvements at the edge to gracefully shed load instead of hard resets
ryan: I'll open an infra bug for token-coalescing (INF-2026-214). devon, can you do the SDK PR to default to jittered backoff?
devon: yep — will target a patch for the SDK tonight and a rollout next week.
jen: customer replied: "Observed improvement, thanks. We'll switch to jittered retries now. Please keep us posted on permanent fixes and billing adjustments."
jen: internal note: recommend support offer a one-time credit for the spike window if we confirm duplicate tokens/billing. tagging billing for review.
alyssa: added billing tag to this thread.
jen: closing loop: will keep this thread open until infra bug and SDK PR are linked. Thanks all for rapid turnaround.
